chief_complaint: sudden excruciating pain and swelling in the left testicle for 2 hours
hpi_details: 21M college student presents with sudden, severe pain and swelling in his left testicle that began 2 hours ago. Pain is accompanied by lower abdominal pain and nausea.
expectations: wants immediate ultrasound and pain relief

core_concepts: Acute unilateral scrotal pain is testicular torsion until proven otherwise; salvage declines with ischemia time, so clinical suspicion requires immediate urology/surgical action.
A high-riding/transverse testis, nausea/vomiting, and absent cremasteric reflex increase suspicion, but no single sign—including Prehn sign—reliably excludes torsion.
Color Doppler ultrasound can support diagnosis only when immediately available and it does not delay exploration; normal/equivocal flow does not override strong clinical suspicion.
Definitive management is urgent scrotal exploration, detorsion, viability assessment, and bilateral orchiopexy; analgesia, NPO status, and surgical consultation must not await imaging.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: sudden excruciating pain and swelling in the left testicle for 2 hours
Key HPI features: 21M college student presents with sudden, severe pain and swelling in his left testicle that began 2 hours ago. Pain is accompanied by lower abdominal pain and nausea.

Objective/Exam findings: Record onset time and vital signs; examine both testes for lie, height, swelling, tenderness, and cremasteric reflex. Obtain Doppler ultrasound only if it will not delay urgent exploration.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Testicular Torsion.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Acute epididymitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Waiting for ultrasound, laboratory results, or response to analgesia when history/examination is strongly concerning for torsion.
Ruling out torsion because Prehn sign is positive, the cremasteric reflex is present, symptoms are intermittent, or pain began more than six hours ago.
Treating presumed epididymitis and arranging outpatient follow-up before urgent surgical assessment of sudden scrotal pain.
Failing to arrange bilateral fixation during operative management because the contralateral bell-clapper risk remains.
management_principles: Activate urgent urology/surgical consultation, keep the patient NPO, establish IV access, and provide analgesia/antiemetic without delaying exploration.
Proceed to immediate exploration when torsion is clinically likely; use Doppler only when it is truly immediate and diagnostic uncertainty remains.
Counsel that manual detorsion is only a temporizing maneuver by an experienced clinician when surgery is not immediately available and never replaces exploration and bilateral orchiopexy.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: Surgical emergency caused by twisting of the spermatic cord, producing acute testicular ischemia.

must_ask.say: Did this severe pain in your scrotum start suddenly, waking you up or while resting?
Along with the testicular pain, have you vomited or felt sick to your stomach?
Does gently lifting your scrotum ease the pain, or does it stay severe?
Did you suffer any hit or trauma to your groin area before the pain started?
Do you have a fever or burning when you urinate?

history.answer: Doctor, my left testicle suddenly started hurting terribly about two hours ago, and it has swollen up.
It started completely out of nowhere about two hours ago while I was just sitting at my desk studying.
The pain is located entirely in my left testicle, not on the right side.
It is an unbearable, twisting, constant pain, easily a nine or ten out of ten in severity.
Yes, the pain shoots upward right into my lower abdomen and my left groin.
No, I have never had sudden testicle pain like this before in my life.
No, trying to support or lift the testicle up does not help at all and actually makes it hurt worse.
I have felt very sick to my stomach from the intense pain, but I haven't actually thrown up.
It swelled up shortly after the pain began, and lying down or standing up doesn't change the size at all.
It is not a dull dragging heaviness, it's just severe sharp pain that stays terrible whether I stand or sit.
No, I never felt any hard lump or painless swelling down there before today.
No fever or chills at all, and it does not burn when I urinate, nor is there any penile discharge.
The left side of the scrotum looks a bit red and swollen, but there are no black patches, blisters, or foul odor.
No, I had no trauma or injury, and I wasn't doing any heavy workout, running, or sexual activity when it struck.
No, I haven't had any mumps, jaw swelling, or swollen salivary glands.
Both of my testicles have always been normally descended in the scrotum, and I've never had any groin surgeries.
No, I haven't lost weight, and I have no back pain, cough, or swelling in my chest.
I have a single steady girlfriend and we always use condoms; I have no other partners.
No, I have never had a urinary catheter, cystoscopy, or any prostate procedures.
We have not been trying to conceive, and I don't have diabetes or any immune problems.
I am terrified that the blood supply is completely choked off and that I might lose my testicle.
I am extremely panicked about the possibility of having to undergo emergency surgery.
I really need something strong for this pain and hope you can do an ultrasound right away to see what is happening.
I have no chronic medical conditions and have always been healthy.
I have never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I am not taking any prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, or supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications or anything else.
I do not smoke cigarettes and I do not vape.
I only drink an occasional beer once or twice a month socially.
I am a 21-year-old college student living in an apartment near campus with a roommate.
No one in my family has had testicular torsion, testicle issues, or urological cancers.

exam.finding: Young male in severe acute distress, pale and diaphoretic, lying curled on the exam table and guarding his left groin.
Blood pressure 135/85 mmHg, pulse 102 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Mild tenderness in the left lower quadrant and suprapubic region, but the abdomen is soft without guarding or rebound tenderness.

Left hemiscrotum is swollen and mildly erythematous; the left testis is high-riding with a transverse lie and exquisite tenderness, the left cremasteric reflex is absent, scrotal elevation does not relieve pain, and transillumination is negative; right testis is normal.
No visible or palpable inguinal bulge or impulse on cough bilaterally, and no inguinal lymphadenopathy.
